dataIdInfo.idPurp: Schema-aware geoprocessing tasks for identifying features near user-supplied reference features.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
Find Features Near Features

A synchronous geoprocessing tool that returns features within a specified geodesic distance of reference features. Use it for questions such as "how many damaged vehicles are within 10 meters of damaged buildings?"

How It Works

The tool filters the input and reference layers when requested, selects input features within the supplied distance of the reference features, and returns the selected features as a feature set. Count the returned records when the question asks "how many."

Parameters

  • Input Features: The features to evaluate, such as damaged vehicles. For REST requests, supply a layer object: {"url":"https://.../FeatureServer/0"}.
  • Input Features Where Clause: Optional SQL filter for the input features.
  • Proximity Features: The reference features, such as damaged buildings. For REST requests, supply a layer object: {"url":"https://.../FeatureServer/0"}.
  • Proximity Features Where Clause: Optional SQL filter for the reference features.
  • Search Distance: A linear distance such as 10 Meters.
  • Output Features: Features from the input layer that meet the proximity condition.

SQL Filter Requirements

Before supplying either SQL where clause, inspect the schema of the selected feature layer. Use the layer's physical field names and verified attribute values; do not use display aliases as SQL field names. The expression must use SQL syntax supported by the referenced feature service.

For example, use DAMAGE_CLASS = 'High Damage Evidence' only after confirming that DAMAGE_CLASS is an actual field and High Damage Evidence is a valid value in that layer. Leave a where clause blank to include all features from that layer.

Example Workflow

  1. Select the vehicle layer as Input Features.
  2. Filter vehicles with a verified vehicle-damage SQL expression.
  3. Select the building layer as Proximity Features.
  4. Filter buildings with a verified high-damage SQL expression.
  5. Set Search Distance to 10 Meters.
  6. Count the returned vehicle features.

Notes

  • The tool uses geodesic distance.
  • Both layers should have compatible spatial references for accurate distance analysis.
  • An invalid SQL expression prevents the tool from running; validate field names and values against the selected layer before execution.
